title: Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
title_zh: 文献研究：Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
summary: Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule in…
abstract: Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule interface. In particular, the role of electrode geometry in determining transport behaviour remains less systematically explored than molecular structure and contact chemistry. Here, we investigate the influence of atomic-scale electrode geometry on the structural, electronic, quantum-transport, thermoelectric, and noise properties of Au–pentane–Au molecular junctions using a combined density functional theory–non-equilibrium Green's function (DFT–NEGF) and machine learning framework. Six representative electrode configurations—Flat Au(111), Pyramidal, Single Apex, Multi-Atom Tip, Nanowire, and Rough Surface—were structurally optimized and systematically compared while maintaining the same pentane molecular backbone and Au–S contact chemistry. The calculations reveal pronounced geometry-dependent variations in Au–S bonding, coordination number, contact area, molecular tilt, charge transfer, electronic-state alignment, and molecule–electrode coupling. These structural and electronic changes directly control quantum transport, with the calculated conductance decreasing from 0.92 G₀ for Flat Au(111) to 0.56 G₀ for the Single Apex configuration. Transmission, current–voltage characteristics, charge redistribution, and interface dipole analysis consistently demonstrate that highly coordinated and extended contacts provide stronger electronic coupling and more efficient transmission pathways. Thermoelectric calculations reveal an opposing trend: lower-coordination contacts exhibit enhanced Seebeck coefficients because of stronger energy dependence of transmission near the Fermi level, whereas the Flat Au(111) junction provides the highest calculated power factor and ZT ≈ 0.68. Shot noise, Fano factor, low-frequency noise, and Hooge-parameter analysis further demonstrate increasing transport fluctuations as electrode coordination decreases. To accelerate transport prediction, a dataset of 1500 configurations were constructed from structural and electronic descriptors extracted from the DFT–NEGF calculations. Among the tested models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance, with a testing R2 of 0.988, RMSE of 0.010 G₀, and MAE of 0.007 G₀. Feature-importance analysis identified Au–S bond length, HOMO–LUMO gap, coupling strength, DOS at the Fermi level, and Au 5d PDOS as the dominant predictors. The trained model successfully predicted conductance for previously unseen electrode configurations, demonstrating its potential for rapid screening of molecular junction structures.

title: High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
title_zh: 文献研究：High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
summary: We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simul…
abstract: We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simultaneously achieving high magnetization and thermodynamic stability. Using this workflow, we systematically explored over 3000 binary (R-T) and ternary (R-T-T ′) compositions spanning R ∈ Y, Sm, T ∈ Fe, Co, Ni, and T ′ ∈ Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, and filtered approximately 240,000 generated crystal structures through machine-learning interatomic potential prescreening and spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) validation. We identify 300+ low-energy magnetic candidates within 0.1 eV/atom above the convex hull at the DFT level, including 5 thermodynamically stable phases. The highest saturation magnetization reaches ∼1.8 T in Fe-rich binary and ternary phases (SmFe 12 , YFe 12 , YFe 18 Ti and Sm 2 Fe 16 Mn). Symmetry analysis reveals that the majority of ternary candidates are subgroup derivatives of known binary prototypes through Wyckoff site splitting that accommodates T ′ substitution. Site-resolved magnetic moment analysis further shows that Mn aligns ferromagnetically with the Fe sublattice with minimal magnetization loss, whereas Cr couples antiferromagnetically, providing systematic guidance for dopant selection. These findings demonstrate a generalizable strategy for targeted magnetic materials discovery and suggest that extending generative searches to larger unit cells (>20 atoms) with higher Fe fractions is a promising route toward stable phases with saturation magnetization exceeding 1.8 T.

title: Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors
title_zh: 文献研究：Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors
summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77985-0 In cuprate superconductors, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, broadban…
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77985-0 In cuprate superconductors, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, broadband optical spectroscopy and DQMC calculations reveal an electronic reconstruction in LSCO beyond x > 0.2, consistent with a checkerboard Zhang–Rice configuration hosting coexisting localized and itinerant carriers.

title: Laser experiments recreate solar flare physics and reveal consistent magnetic reconnection rates
title_zh: 文献研究：Laser experiments recreate solar flare physics and reveal consistent magnetic reconnection rates
summary: Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the u…
abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the underlying mechanism behind cosmic events such as solar flares and substorms in Earth's magnetosphere.

title: Polarization-coupled complete operators in sliding ferroelectric semiconductors for native in-memory attention computing
title_zh: 文献研究：Polarization-coupled complete operators in sliding ferroelectric semiconductors for native in-memory attention computing
summary: Attention computing, central to Transformer-based generative AI, calls for native in-memory hardware with linear and nonlinear operators intrinsically coupled. Current compute-in-memory (CIM), however…
abstract: Attention computing, central to Transformer-based generative AI, calls for native in-memory hardware with linear and nonlinear operators intrinsically coupled. Current compute-in-memory (CIM), however, remains tailored to linear algebra, lacking integrated nonlinear operators. Here, we demonstrate complete-operator hardware that intrinsically couples both operator types in situ via ferroelectric polarization. Our device integrates a vertical ferroelectric tunnel junction for linear multiply-accumulate operations and a lateral ferroelectric semiconductor field-effect transistor for exponential functions in sliding-ferroelectric semiconductor ReS2. Tuning lateral transport length and vertical barrier thickness yields designable exponential operators with tunable sensitivity and operating range. A fabricated (9×3)×9 array realizes the first in-memory hardware execution of full Transformer attention primitives, including intrinsic Softmax, with device-level 600-ps latency and 320-aJ/operation energy. A closed-loop hardware prototype enables real-time text generation, with experimentally calibrated simulations supporting neural-signal-to-language scalability. This work embeds the missing nonlinearity directly into memory, advancing CIM toward complete, native hardware for generative AI.
